units.note: Minor: 'from which they could both attack and remain secure' adds 'attack'; Greek has only δυναμένας σφίσιν ἀσφάλειαν παρέχεσθαι. Not sense-inverting; not flagged.

findings.quote: Claudius’ son, though wounded, only barely and unexpectedly escaped the danger.
findings.problem: Greek ends with an accusative object clause (καὶ τὸν υἱὸν τοῦ Κλαυδίου τραυματίαν, μόλις καὶ παραδόξως τὸν κίνδυνον διαπεφευγότα) followed by a lacuna marker ***; the governing verb is lost. English supplies a finite verb and closes the sentence as if the text were whole.
findings.proposed_fix: As for Claudius’ son, wounded, who had barely and unexpectedly escaped the danger, [gap in the text]

units.note: Lacuna smoothed over; mark it, do not supply the missing verb.

Final sentence is a separate fragment (Greek has a dash break and begins οἱ δὲ, 'But/And they'); English 'Then they' implies sequence with the Hannibal passage. Context of καταρράκτας passage is unknown and ἐπεβάλοντο is ambiguous, so no fix proposed.
